text:
Charle-Edouard D'Astous went undrafted, took the long road through Sweden (39 points in 49 SHL games for Brynäs in 2024-25), and is now running real minutes on Tampa Bay's blue line. He has 14 points in 21 games, seven of them on the power play, and his ice time over the last ten games is up almost four minutes a night to about 20. That's a coach telling you something.

Some of the scoring will cool. He has four goals on 2.2 expected, and the Lightning have shot well above their chances while he's out there. Our talent range puts his true scoring rate closer to 1.5 points per 60 than the 2.2 he's running. But the play underneath is good: Tampa takes 58.6% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season too, 86th percentile among defensemen. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the reason: 60% of his exits leave the zone with possession.

Watch the minutes. If they stay near 20 when the bounces even out, he's a regular, not a hot month.
